title: New ECAs: 0.10% sulphur in the Canadian Arctic and Norwegian Sea from 1 March 2027

scenes.label: REGULATION UPDATE
scenes.heading: Two new ECAs. One deadline: 1 March 2027.
scenes.narration: From the 1st of March 2027, two more sea areas will demand 0.10% sulphur fuel. Is your ship ready?

scenes.label: WHAT CHANGED?
scenes.heading: Canadian Arctic and Norwegian Sea are now ECAs
scenes.body: Amendments to MARPOL Annex VI, resolution MEPC.392(82), entered into force on 1 March 2026.
scenes.narration: What changed? The Canadian Arctic and the Norwegian Sea are now Emission Control Areas under MARPOL Annex VI, in force since the 1st of March 2026.

scenes.label: WHY?
scenes.heading: Cleaner air in sensitive waters
scenes.body: ECAs cut sulphur oxides, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter from ship exhaust.
scenes.narration: Why? Emission Control Areas cut sulphur oxides, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter from ship exhaust.

scenes.label: WHEN?
scenes.heading: Two dates to know

items.title: In force. NOx Tier III by build date

scenes.narration: When? The nitrogen oxide Tier III rules already apply to newer ships, depending on their build dates. The sulphur limit follows twelve months later, on the 1st of March 2027.

scenes.label: WHO IS AFFECTED?
scenes.heading: Every ship operating in these areas
scenes.body: Fuel sulphur must not exceed 0.10% m/m, unless an approved equivalent such as an exhaust gas cleaning system is used.
scenes.narration: Who is affected? Every ship operating there. Fuel must not exceed 0.10% sulphur, unless an approved equivalent such as an exhaust gas cleaning system is used.

scenes.label: WHAT MUST THE SHIP DO?
scenes.heading: Before you enter

items.title: Plot the ECA limits in the passage plan
Secure compliant fuel in good time
Log date, time, position, tank volumes

scenes.narration: What must the ship do? Plot the ECA limits in your passage plan. Secure compliant fuel early. Follow your written fuel changeover procedure, and log the changeover with date, time, position and tank volumes.
Stay updated with the maritime industry. Follow HeyMariner.
